name: mode_real Operating mode
description: Operating mode the heat pump reports; the climate entity reads it and writes 2 when it switches heating on from another mode.
guidance: The Trianco S300 manual lists Standard, Eco, Vacation, Intelligent and High demand. On an Indol PV300 with the same product ID, 0 = Intelligent, 2 = Eco (heat pump only), 3 = heat pump plus heater after the delay (Standard here) and 4 = heat pump plus heater at once (High demand); those labels are used here but aren't confirmed on the S300. The climate entity shows all of them as heat and doesn't change the mode when heating is already on.

name: M17 Fan after heating

description: What the fan does once the water has reached its target temperature: run at low speed, run at high speed, or stop (Trianco S300 manual). It is the app's Ventilation switch and Air Speed knob.
guidance: A ventilation setting: Low or High keeps air moving through the unit after heating stops, Off lets the fan stop. While heating the controller runs the fan itself, so this doesn't change the fan speed during heating or the efficiency. The climate entity's fan modes write the same code.

name: D01 Defrost start temperature
description: Coil temperature (T04) below which a defrost can start.
guidance: Defrost starts when the coil (T04) is below D01 and at least D03 minutes have passed since the last one. It ends when T04 reaches D02 or after D04 minutes, and lasts at least D05 minutes (PHNIX manuals). During a defrost the compressor keeps running and the fan stops (Trianco S300 manual). A lower D01 means fewer, later defrosts. Change it only if the coil ices up or defrosts too often.

name: D02 Defrost end temperature
description: Coil temperature (T04) at which a defrost ends.
guidance: Defrost starts when the coil (T04) is below D01 and at least D03 minutes have passed since the last one. It ends when T04 reaches D02 or after D04 minutes, and lasts at least D05 minutes (PHNIX manuals). During a defrost the compressor keeps running and the fan stops (Trianco S300 manual). A higher D02 clears the ice more thoroughly but lasts longer.

name: D03 Defrost interval
description: Minimum time between two defrosts. The app calls it 'Duration of defrosting', but a 30-90 minute range only makes sense as the interval, as in the PHNIX manuals.
guidance: Defrost starts when the coil (T04) is below D01 and at least D03 minutes have passed since the last one. It ends when T04 reaches D02 or after D04 minutes, and lasts at least D05 minutes (PHNIX manuals). During a defrost the compressor keeps running and the fan stops (Trianco S300 manual).

name: D04 Maximum defrost time
description: Longest a defrost may last.
guidance: Defrost starts when the coil (T04) is below D01 and at least D03 minutes have passed since the last one. It ends when T04 reaches D02 or after D04 minutes, and lasts at least D05 minutes (PHNIX manuals). During a defrost the compressor keeps running and the fan stops (Trianco S300 manual).

name: D05 Minimum defrost time
description: Shortest a defrost lasts.
guidance: Defrost starts when the coil (T04) is below D01 and at least D03 minutes have passed since the last one. It ends when T04 reaches D02 or after D04 minutes, and lasts at least D05 minutes (PHNIX manuals). During a defrost the compressor keeps running and the fan stops (Trianco S300 manual).

name: D06 Defrost method
description: How defrosts are started.
guidance: Standard uses D01-D05; Intelligent also uses D07. What Economic changes isn't documented. Your heat pump reports 0 = Standard; 1 and 2 follow the app's order.

name: D07 Intelligent defrost threshold
description: Threshold used by intelligent defrosting (D06 = Intelligent).
guidance: Not documented; it probably compares the ambient and coil temperatures. It only matters with D06 = Intelligent. Leave it unchanged.

name: E01 EEV control mode
description: Whether the electronic expansion valve (EEV) regulates itself (Automatic) or not (Manual). 1 = Automatic is confirmed by the PHNIX PC1001 manual; the app lists the options in a different order.
guidance: Keep Automatic. In Manual the valve no longer follows the superheat target E02, which can return liquid refrigerant to the compressor or starve the coil.

name: E02 Target superheat
description: Superheat the EEV aims for: suction minus coil temperature (T05 - T04).
guidance: Compare it with the Superheat sensor. A higher target closes the valve further (less refrigerant, safer for the compressor, less heat); a lower one opens it. Change it only with an installer: too little superheat can return liquid to the compressor.

name: E03 EEV start position
description: EEV opening when the compressor starts.
guidance: The valve starts at E03 (O07 reads 240 at start-up) and then regulates towards E02.

name: E04 EEV minimum position
description: Smallest opening the EEV may regulate down to.
guidance: Your EEV often sits at this minimum because the measured superheat is below E02. Lowering E04 lets it close further and reduces the refrigerant flow; don't change it to chase the superheat reading without an installer.

name: E05 EEV defrost position
description: EEV opening during defrost.
guidance: O07 reads this value (480) during defrost and while the compressor is stopped.

name: G01 Disinfection temperature
description: Water temperature the disinfection cycle heats to.
guidance: Disinfection (anti-legionella) heats the water to G01 every G04 days at G03 o'clock and holds it for G02 minutes. G02 = 0, as on your heat pump, most likely means it never runs. Above 60 °C (the limit of R01) the booster is probably needed.

name: G02 Disinfection duration
description: How long the water is held at G01.
guidance: Disinfection (anti-legionella) heats the water to G01 every G04 days at G03 o'clock and holds it for G02 minutes. G02 = 0, as on your heat pump, most likely means it never runs. Above 60 °C (the limit of R01) the booster is probably needed.

name: G03 Disinfection start hour
description: Hour of the day the disinfection starts.
guidance: Disinfection (anti-legionella) heats the water to G01 every G04 days at G03 o'clock and holds it for G02 minutes. G02 = 0, as on your heat pump, most likely means it never runs. Above 60 °C (the limit of R01) the booster is probably needed.

name: G04 Disinfection interval
description: Days between disinfection cycles.
guidance: Disinfection (anti-legionella) heats the water to G01 every G04 days at G03 o'clock and holds it for G02 minutes. G02 = 0, as on your heat pump, most likely means it never runs. Above 60 °C (the limit of R01) the booster is probably needed.

name: H01 Remember power state
app_name: Remember the power status of device when power down
description: Whether the heat pump returns to its previous on/off state after a power cut.
guidance: YES restarts heating after a power cut if it was on before. Keep YES unless it should stay off.

name: H03 Heating source
description: Type of heat source. The app only offers Air source.

name: H07 Temperature unit
description: Unit the heat pump reports temperatures in.
guidance: The Temperature Unit select in Home Assistant must match it. If you change H07 in the app, change the select as well.

name: H30 Device address
description: Address of the controller on its communication bus.
guidance: Read-only: a wrong address can cut the controller off from the Wi-Fi module.

name: H31 Control mode

guidance: Must stay on DTU&WIFI for the app and Home Assistant to work, so it is read-only.

name: H32 Cloud upload interval
app_name: Circle of submitting data to Cloud
description: Minutes between the heat pump's own uploads to the cloud.
guidance: Your heat pump uses 1 minute. Home Assistant reads the cloud every 5 minutes, so a larger value only makes the readings older. Keep 1.

name: H98 Model selection
description: Hardware model the controller is configured for.
guidance: Never change it: it tells the controller which hardware it drives. Your heat pump reports 2, which the app shows as 0X08. The cloud declares a range of 2-3, which supports 3 = 0X18, but that isn't confirmed.

name: H99 Display temperature compensation

name: R01 Target water temperature
description: Target water temperature, the main control. The climate entity sets the same value.
guidance: Heating starts when the controlling sensor (T02 bottom, or T03 top with R17 = YES) drops R03 below R01, and stops at R01. Each change is probably stored in the controller's memory, which allows a limited number of writes (see T12), so avoid automations that change R01 every few minutes.

name: R03 Start hysteresis (bottom sensor)
app_name: Hysteresis of heat pump startup(bottom sensor)
description: How far below R01 the bottom sensor (T02) must drop before heating restarts.
guidance: A small value keeps the water closer to R01 but starts the compressor more often; very small values cause short cycling. Your heat pump uses 5.0 °C.

name: R04 Use R05 as booster setpoint
app_name: Enable R05 as setpoint of booster?
description: Whether the booster heats to its own setpoint R05 instead of R01.
guidance: Electric heater logic (Trianco S300 manual): in Standard mode the heater starts if the target isn't reached after R06 minutes; in High demand mode it starts without the delay; in Eco mode it never starts; both decide with the R03 differential. Intelligent mode picks Eco above R10 ambient (T01), Standard between R09 and R10 and High demand between R08 and R09; with R07 = YES the heater presumably replaces the heat pump below R08. The heater output is O02. Only relevant with an electric heater fitted.

name: R05 Booster setpoint
description: Water temperature the booster heats to when R04 = YES.
guidance: Electric heater logic (Trianco S300 manual): in Standard mode the heater starts if the target isn't reached after R06 minutes; in High demand mode it starts without the delay; in Eco mode it never starts; both decide with the R03 differential. Intelligent mode picks Eco above R10 ambient (T01), Standard between R09 and R10 and High demand between R08 and R09; with R07 = YES the heater presumably replaces the heat pump below R08. The heater output is O02. Only relevant with an electric heater fitted.

name: R06 Booster start delay
description: How long the heat pump runs before the booster may help. The cloud declares a range of 0-90 for the app's 0-450 minutes, so the heat pump most likely stores it in 5-minute units; Home Assistant writes it in steps of 5.
guidance: Electric heater logic (Trianco S300 manual): in Standard mode the heater starts if the target isn't reached after R06 minutes; in High demand mode it starts without the delay; in Eco mode it never starts; both decide with the R03 differential. Intelligent mode picks Eco above R10 ambient (T01), Standard between R09 and R10 and High demand between R08 and R09; with R07 = YES the heater presumably replaces the heat pump below R08. The heater output is O02. Only relevant with an electric heater fitted.

name: R07 Booster replaces heat pump
description: Whether the booster takes over from the heat pump below the R08 ambient temperature.
guidance: Electric heater logic (Trianco S300 manual): in Standard mode the heater starts if the target isn't reached after R06 minutes; in High demand mode it starts without the delay; in Eco mode it never starts; both decide with the R03 differential. Intelligent mode picks Eco above R10 ambient (T01), Standard between R09 and R10 and High demand between R08 and R09; with R07 = YES the heater presumably replaces the heat pump below R08. The heater output is O02. Only relevant with an electric heater fitted. With YES and no booster fitted, the heat pump presumably stops heating below R08 (-5.0 °C on your unit).

app_name: Setpoint of ambient temp to activate booster to replace heatpump
description: Lower ambient temperature (T01) limit of the High demand band of Intelligent mode; below it the electric heater presumably replaces the heat pump (R07 = YES).
guidance: Electric heater logic (Trianco S300 manual): in Standard mode the heater starts if the target isn't reached after R06 minutes; in High demand mode it starts without the delay; in Eco mode it never starts; both decide with the R03 differential. Intelligent mode picks Eco above R10 ambient (T01), Standard between R09 and R10 and High demand between R08 and R09; with R07 = YES the heater presumably replaces the heat pump below R08. The heater output is O02. Only relevant with an electric heater fitted.

guidance: Electric heater logic (Trianco S300 manual): in Standard mode the heater starts if the target isn't reached after R06 minutes; in High demand mode it starts without the delay; in Eco mode it never starts; both decide with the R03 differential. Intelligent mode picks Eco above R10 ambient (T01), Standard between R09 and R10 and High demand between R08 and R09; with R07 = YES the heater presumably replaces the heat pump below R08. The heater output is O02. Only relevant with an electric heater fitted.

Intelligent mode picks Eco above R10 ambient (T01), Standard between R09 and R10 and High demand between R08 and R09; with R07 = YES the heater presumably replaces the heat pump below R08. The heater output is O02. Only relevant with an electric heater fitted.

name: T01 Ambient temperature

guidance: The booster settings R08-R10 and the compressor limit R12 compare against it.

name: T02 Bottom water temperature (return)
description: Water temperature at the controller's bottom sensor. The controller is made for a tank with bottom and top sensors; on your installation it is on the return pipe.
guidance: With R17 = NO this sensor controls heating: it starts when T02 is R03 below R01.

name: T03 Top water temperature (flow)
description: Water temperature at the controller's top sensor; on your installation the flow pipe.
guidance: T03 - T02 is the Water ΔT sensor. T10 showed the same value as T03 throughout your log.

name: T04 Coil temperature
description: Temperature of the evaporator coil, the coil the air passes through.
guidance: Defrost starts and ends on this temperature (D01, D02). It is also the reference for the superheat (T05 - T04).

name: T05 Suction temperature
description: Refrigerant temperature in the suction pipe, the gas going from the coil to the compressor. It is not an air temperature.
guidance: With E01 = Automatic the EEV keeps T05 - T04 (superheat) at E02. When T05 stays well below T04, as in your log (about -13 °C against 0 °C), the superheat is negative and the EEV closes to its minimum E04. The data can't tell whether that comes from the sensor placement or the refrigerant circuit; ask an installer rather than changing E02 or E04.

name: T10 Displayed water temperature

guidance: Equal to T03 throughout your log.

guidance: Your installation has no solar circuit, yet T06 rose from about 63 to 87 °C while the compressor ran and dropped when it stopped. That fits the compressor discharge (hot gas) temperature, but it isn't confirmed.

name: T07 Discharge temperature (unconfirmed)
description: Not shown in the app.
guidance: On an Indol PV300 with the same product ID (github.com/victor987/hitemp), it read 59 °C and was taken to be the compressor discharge temperature.

name: T09 Compressor temperature (unconfirmed)
description: Not shown in the app.
guidance: On an Indol PV300 with the same product ID (github.com/victor987/hitemp), it read 30-40 °C and dropped when the compressor started.

name: Superheat (T05 - T04)
description: Suction minus coil temperature (T05 - T04), calculated by Home Assistant.
guidance: The value E02 targets. Negative values mean the suction pipe reads colder than the coil, which keeps the EEV at E04.

name: Water ΔT (T03 - T02)
description: Top minus bottom water temperature (T03 - T02), calculated by Home Assistant.
guidance: On your installation, how much the water warms up through the heat pump. Heat pumps are usually designed for about 5 °C; a much larger value can mean low water flow.
